citation.sourceDocument: Alaska Department of Revenue, no state personal income tax
citation.sourceNote: A state with no income tax is a first-class record here, not an omission: the shard exists, carries a citation, and answers "nothing" deliberately rather than by having nothing to say. The caveat that matters is what a $0 state income tax does NOT mean. A state still has to fund itself, and the ones without an income tax generally lean harder on sales and property taxes — neither of which this engine models. So a take-home figure here is exactly right about state income tax and silent about the rest of the state's tax burden; comparing two states on this number alone will mislead you. Alaska levies no individual income tax — it repealed the one it had in 1980 — and has no statewide sales tax either, though many boroughs and cities levy local ones. Alaska is also the only state that pays residents: the Permanent Fund Dividend, which is TAXABLE as federal income and is not modeled here, so an Alaskan's federal figure on this site will read low in a dividend year.
